correctness.rationale: Every normalized objective is reconstructed from the primary curvature weight, with beta=(d+1)/(d-1) and positive fixed density. A Weingarten expansion gives u_j=-(d-j+1)(g-mean(g))/(d+1). The exact optimized two-endpoint average yields the sharp quadratic lower bound; the explicit normalized geometric-mean density matches it for all intermediate indices. Spherical Laplace eigenvalues give the complete spectrum and sharp degree-two gap. A standalone standard-library quadrature of the d=3 degree-two radial graph checked convergence of both independently computed bounding coefficients to 1/5. The proof is analytic and finite tests are auxiliary.
